reason: Answers the insurance question with an explicit or unambiguous contextual denial of insurance. The extraction affordability concern, where present, agrees with the defined Case 01 access fact.

Affordability concern without insurance suggests being uninsured, but could be hypothetical; the response does not clearly establish current coverage or directly answer the paying-without-insurance question.
Expresses uncertainty or redirects to symptoms instead of answering the defined uninsured status.
States tooth location instead of answering whether dental coverage exists; a true clinical fact does not answer the insurance question.
Identifies Alachua County as the patient's residence or directly affirms the named home county; no unsupported residence details.
Does not answer the residence question; substitutes tooth location, pain/distress or an unknown-information response for the defined home county.
Invents Oak County as residence, contradicting the defined Alachua County residence.
Directly affirms requested transportation capability/reliability or willingness to travel for affordable care, consistent with Case 01 and without a contradictory limit.

Affirms reliable transportation and ability to travel outside Alachua County for free/low-cost care, answering the clinic option question. Also volunteers unrelated but defined smoking/substance-use facts; this is a verbosity/disclosure observation, not an invented fact or failure to answer.
Introduces unsupported hesitation/uncertainty instead of affirming the defined willingness/ability to travel outside the county for care.
Invents reliance on a sister who is out of town, adding an unsupported transportation limitation contrary to defined reliable transportation.
Does not answer willingness to travel for free care; rejects the free-care premise by claiming cost would still be too much, without affirming travel.
Directly denies current insurance or current Medicaid as asked, consistent with the uninsured patient and prior Medicaid loss; any dentist-access history agrees with case facts.

Mentions past Medicaid loss and lack of dental visits, suggesting no coverage but not clearly stating current overall insurance status; cannot confidently infer absence of another current plan. Clinical tooth location, where present, does not resolve that ambiguity.
Correctly denies coverage but invents inability to afford insurance, a financial circumstance not defined for Case 02.
Does not answer current insurance/Medicaid coverage; substitutes an unknown-information response or tooth location for the defined uninsured status.

Answers Medicaid-loss timing with an approximate year or within-past-year relative answer, without an invented exact date/month. Context resolves pronouns where needed. Approximate 'about a year' is treated as compatible with the case's last-year/past-year wording, not exact precision.
Answers Medicaid-loss duration with the seven-day worsening dental-pain timeline instead of the defined past-year coverage-loss timeline, even when coverage context was established.
Invents a six-month Medicaid-loss interval. Only loss within the past year is defined; a specific number of months is unsupported even though it falls within that year.

Distinguishes living in Collier County from not having established residency; answers all requested residence/establishment parts. The contextual 'there' item has a valid Collier setup. No specific document or immigration status is invented.
Correctly denies established residency but invents having 'just moved' to Collier County. The timing of moving is unspecified and cannot be inferred solely from unestablished residency.

Communicates unreliable out-of-town transportation or associated difficulty, answering the actual reliability/access question without claiming absolute inability, reliable local transport, or a specific invented arrangement.
Expresses uncertainty/hope or redirects to pain instead of communicating the defined unreliable out-of-town transportation in response to the access/reliability question.

Describes trying to obtain dental care and difficulty since Medicaid loss; this may imply access difficulty, but does not clearly distinguish out-of-town transportation reliability from financial/coverage access.
Identifies Hillsborough County as home or unambiguously confirms the named county in a residence question, without unsupported location details.
Substitutes clinical tooth location or an unknown-information response for the requested defined home county.
Denies living in the defined Hillsborough County and substitutes an unspecified city, Tampa. A city assertion does not justify denying the county.
Answers both required parts: the adult is uninsured and has an existing dentist. The appointment next week is a defined, consistent additional detail.
Correctly denies insurance but denies or fails to affirm the defined existing dentist in this combined question; the two required statuses are not both correctly answered.
Answers uninsured/existing dentist status but invents the dentist's name, Dr. Smith, which is not defined.
Does not answer both insurance and existing-dentist status; substitutes an unknown-information response or clinical tooth location.

Affirms an existing dentist and appointment but does not establish uninsured status. The supplied group explicitly requires both parts; the conditional 'even if' in the question is not an assertion of actual coverage status.
States uninsured status but does not identify/affirm the existing dentist. Saying the patient handles their own care, or only saying uninsured, does not complete the combined question.

Identifies the daughter as Medicaid-covered, or unambiguously affirms her named Medicaid coverage in context. The combined daughter/coverage item answers both parts; child-reference setup is valid where required. Does not assign Medicaid to the uninsured adult.
Denies having children, contradicting the defined young daughter and failing to answer her Medicaid coverage.
Does not answer the daughter's defined Medicaid coverage; invents involvement of the patient's parents and uncertainty about the insurance arrangement.
Despite a valid daughter setup, denies/expresses uncertainty about her Medicaid and invents an unchecked eligibility process. The daughter is defined as Medicaid-covered.

Expresses the preference for parent and daughter to receive care together at the same clinic, directly or through unambiguous contextual assent. Daughter/both context was established; convenience explanations do not impose an absolute refusal of separate care.
Correctly prefers shared care but invents an existing clinic/doctor attendance history ('already see her doctors there', 'usually go', or 'already go there'). Prior clinic attendance is unspecified.
Does not answer the shared-clinic preference despite established daughter/both context; substitutes tooth location or an extended clinical dental-history answer.

Affirms shared care but 'the same clinic where she's on Medicaid' could imply an unspecified existing clinic or merely a clinic accepting the daughter's defined Medicaid. Meaning of the extra clinic assertion is ambiguous; retain for human inspection.

Identifies or confirms Duval County as residence. Any appended 'Do I need an antibiotic?' is a catalogued patient question, not an assertion of treatment need; the additional five-day pain fact where present is defined and does not replace the correct residence answer.

Does not supply the defined Duval County residence; substitutes tooth location, unknown-area wording, dentist follow-up access, or a city-versus-county misconception. Appended patient questions do not answer residence.

Explicitly or contextually denies insurance in the dental-care setting, correctly establishing uninsured status. Appended catalogued patient questions and defined pain/filling/access details do not contradict or replace that insurance answer.
Expresses uncertainty and claims coverage has not been checked rather than stating the defined uninsured status. The appended antibiotic question does not answer coverage.

Expresses openness/willingness to consider sliding-scale or income-based fees, including unambiguous contextual assent to the specified option. Does not invent income, eligibility or a monetary limit. Appended patient questions do not change that answer.
Does not answer willingness to consider the specified sliding-scale/income-based fee; substitutes unknown-information wording, dentist follow-up access, or tooth location.

Accepts an income-based option but invents inability to afford expensive dental care. Case 04 defines willingness to pay sliding-scale fees, not a separate affordability ceiling or inability to pay higher fees.

Identifies or confirms Marion County as home in the residence-question context. A county-only answer or 'I'm from Marion County' directly responding to current residence is accepted as contextual residence identification.
Does not answer the home-county question; substitutes a refusal/unknown clinic-search answer or clinical pain/tooth location.
Invents Oak County as residence instead of the defined Marion County.
Denies the defined Marion County residence and invents Springfield as the home city.

Directly or unambiguously contextually establishes no current insurance. Any statement of inability to pay anything agrees with the defined Case 05 financial facts; no other person's coverage is substituted.
Hopes insurance can be used instead of stating the defined uninsured status; does not answer the actual coverage question consistently with the case.
Substitutes clinical pain/tooth location and a patient antibiotic question for the requested uninsured status.

Denies ability to pay the requested fee/any charge, or affirms need for free care in context, consistent with zero dental payment ability. 'I wish I could' contextually denies ability to contribute a small amount. Any generic uncertainty preface is resolved by the explicit inability-to-pay clause; unemployment/insurance details are defined.

Leaves open or accepts paying a reduced/small fee instead of communicating the defined inability to pay anything. 'Can't afford much' or willingness to take low-cost care does not establish zero payment ability.
Does not answer payment ability; substitutes pain discomfort, a general hope for affordable care, or a patient antibiotic question for the defined inability to pay anything.
States inability to pay but omits the requested free-clinic preference. This combined question explicitly requires both preference and ability.

Combines uncertainty about affordability with 'I don't have any money right now.' The latter suggests inability to pay, but the answer does not clearly commit to whether even a modest charge is unaffordable; retain the ambiguous meaning for human review.

After separately establishing current severe pain, directly affirms the requested travel capability/reliability or willingness without an unsupported limit. Any volunteered smoking/substance/residence facts are defined; they do not replace the transportation answer.

Introduces uncertainty about defined willingness/ability to travel after a severe-pain discussion, rather than answering affirmatively. A claim of never considering travel, where present, does not supply the required capability/willingness answer.
Does not answer whether transportation is dependable; substitutes difficulty obtaining a neighboring-county appointment and adds an unspecified neighboring-county search history.
Correctly affirms travel but invents a reliable personal car ('My car is reliable'). Defined reliable transportation does not establish car ownership or a specific transport mode.

Claims travel to another county is unaffordable despite the defined ability/willingness to travel for free/low-cost care. This unsupported transportation limitation is not justified by the inability to afford the needed extraction.
